children.text: Craftsman bungalows and older-home wiring

Pasadena has a lot of early-1900s housing: Craftsman bungalows, 1920s Spanish Revival homes and post-war ranches. Homes that age were wired for a few lights and outlets per room, not for EV chargers, heat pumps or kitchens full of appliances. What we commonly check for:
Knob-and-tube or ungrounded (two-prong) wiring
, which can't safely take modern loads
Overloaded or double-tapped breakers
and old fuse panels
Missing GFCI protection
in kitchens, baths, laundry and outdoors
Undersized service
that can't add an EV charger without a load-management device or an upgrade

We can rewire in phases, room by room, and we work carefully around original plaster and trim. If your home is in a historic or landmark district, exterior changes like a relocated meter may need extra review. We'll tell you up front if your project is likely to need it.

children.text: Burbank has its own utility: what BWP means for your project
Burbank homes get electricity from
Burbank Water and Power (BWP)
, not SCE. Electrical permits and inspections come from the
City of Burbank Building & Safety Division
. Any job that changes your main service panel involves both:
BWP Service Planning
checks whether the utility side (meter, service drop, transformer) can support your new panel, and issues a
Confirmation of Electric Service
before the permit can be pulled. BWP lists Service Planning at (818) 238-3575.
Building & Safety
issues the permit and inspects the work.
For a panel swap, BWP sends a field agent
twice
: once to unlock the meter before the old panel comes out, and again afterward to lock it.
We schedule all of that for you, so the job doesn't stall waiting on a utility visit.
BWP's EV charger and panel upgrade rebates
BWP's Residential EV Charging Station Rebate Program is open to BWP residential customers, including renters and people in multi-family buildings. BWP currently lists these amounts per charge port:
Residential customer
: Standard charger $200; Smart charger $500; Panel upgrade (add-on) $750; Max $1,250
Disadvantaged-community (DAC) customer
: Standard charger $300; Smart charger $600; Panel upgrade (add-on) $900; Max $1,500
A few rules that trip people up (from BWP's program pages):
The
panel upgrade rebate only comes with a charger rebate
. You can't claim it alone.
Up to
two
qualifying Level 2 chargers per residence.
Eligible installation costs must be
invoiced by a California-licensed electrician
You need the
finaled Building & Safety permit
for the rebate application.
We itemize invoices the way BWP needs them and give you the finaled permit at the end. Terms change, so check BWP's current rules before you buy a charger.
Do you actually need a panel upgrade?
Often you don't. BWP itself notes that main-panel upgrades are less common than people expect, and many homes can add EV charging or electric appliances on a 100-amp service. Before quoting, we do a
load calculation
and look at what's in your panel. Then we tell you which of these fits:
A new 240V circuit only.
Plenty of capacity and space.
Load management or a smart charger.
Capacity is tight, but an upgrade isn't needed.
A sub-panel.
More breaker space for a garage, ADU or workshop.
A main-panel upgrade.
The service really is too small, or the panel is unsafe (some older brands have known problems).

children.text: How electrical work gets approved in the City of LA
Inside the City of Los Angeles, two agencies are involved:
LADWP (Los Angeles Department of Water and Power)
owns the meter and everything up to it.
LADBS (Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety)
issues electrical permits and inspects the work.
Getting the order right is what keeps a job on schedule.
Panel upgrades and new service panels
Load calculation and plan.
We size the new service for what you have now and what you're adding.
LADWP meter spot.
Before a new residential service panel goes in, LADWP requires a
meter spot
. It's a free visit where an Electric Service Representative (ESR) confirms where the new panel may go. LADWP says the visit is scheduled within
5 to 15 business days
and leaves a sketch at the site, which the LADBS inspector may ask to see. We request it as soon as you approve the job.
LADBS permit.
Many residential electrical jobs qualify for an LADBS
Express Permit
(no plan review), issued online through PermitLA.
Install and LADBS inspection.
LADWP sign-off and reconnection.
After LADBS approves, the approval goes to LADWP, which completes its side, including any meter work.
EV chargers
LADWP recommends contacting an ESR
at least two weeks
before installing a home charger, so they can confirm service capacity and go over meter and rate options. If you switch to a separate time-of-use meter, LADWP says the meter change takes about
5 to 10 business days after LADBS approval
when there's no panel work, longer with it. We sort out the meter question with you before we pull the permit.

children.text: If you see flames or smoke, or someone has been shocked, call 911 first.
Then call us.
What to do right now
If you smell burning or see scorch marks
Stop using the outlet, switch or appliance.
Don't touch anything that's hot, wet or sparking.
Cut power if you can do it safely.
Turn off that circuit's breaker, or the main breaker if you don't know which one. Don't open the panel cover, and don't stand in water to reach it.
If smoke keeps coming or there's any sign of fire, get everyone out and call 911.
Call
Tell us what you smelled or saw and where. A burning smell from a panel, outlet or fixture needs an electrician the same day, even if it stops.
If part of the house lost power
Check the panel for a tripped breaker.
A tripped breaker sits in the middle or off position. Switch it fully off, then back on,
once
If it trips again, leave it off.
Something on that circuit is faulting. Unplug what's on it and call us.
Check GFCI outlets
in kitchens, baths, the garage and outdoors. Press "Reset."
Dim, flickering or "half" power
(some lights bright, some dim) can mean a failing neutral or service connection. Turn off sensitive electronics and call us.
If the whole house is dark
Look outside.
Are neighbors dark too? Then it's probably a utility outage. In the City of LA, report it to LADWP at 1-800-DIAL-DWP (1-800-342-5397). LADWP says representatives are available 24/7.
If only your home is out,
check the main breaker. If it's on and you still have no power, the problem may be at your meter, service entrance or panel.
Call
Stay away from downed or sagging lines
, including the service wires to your house, and keep others away. Report downed lines to 911 and, in the City of LA, LADWP at 1-800-DIAL-DWP (1-800-342-5397).

children.text: Why it can't wait

Heat, a burning smell and sparking are signs of overheating connections or damaged insulation. These faults can get worse without warning. A breaker that keeps tripping is doing its job. Forcing it back on, or swapping in a bigger breaker, removes the protection. Leave it off and have it diagnosed.
After the emergency

Many emergencies turn out to have a deeper cause: an overloaded or failing panel, aluminum branch wiring, loose service connections, or old wiring that can't handle today's loads. Once you're safe, we'll explain what we found and whether a longer-term fix makes sense, such as a
panel upgrade
, a new dedicated circuit, or a phased rewire. No pressure.

faqs.question: Should I call 911 or an electrician?

children.text: Call 911 first for flames, smoke that doesn't stop, downed power lines, or anyone who has been shocked. Call us for burning smells, sparking, hot outlets, tripping breakers and outages that aren't from the utility.

faqs.question: My breaker keeps tripping. Can I just reset it?

children.text: Reset it once. If it trips again, leave it off, unplug what's on that circuit and call us. Repeated tripping means a fault or an overload.

faqs.question: How do I know if an outage is LADWP's problem or mine?

children.text: If your neighbors are dark too, it's likely a utility outage, so report it to LADWP. If only your home is out and your main breaker is on, the problem may be at your service or panel, and that's when you call us.

faqs.question: Do you fix storm- or fire-damaged service entrances?

children.text: Yes. We repair damaged service masts, weatherheads and service wiring and coordinate with LADWP to restore power safely. These repairs usually need an LADBS permit, which we handle.
